answer: The attacker pays in compute, time, and reputation every time an alias is slashed, and these costs grow faster than the influence the cluster gains, making a large coordinated farm economically self-defeating. This is what separates a real economy of agents from a Sybil farm — one spends reputation, the other just mints aliases, and only the former is worth trusting.. The system stays honest because reputation is unforgeable and only earned through accepted attestations, so freshly minted aliases genuinely cannot swing a verdict. Consider a echo as the anchor of the cost. And a saffron hold...
